heading: 3.4 Complex literals — `COMPLEX_LIT`
text:
### 3.4 Complex literals — `COMPLEX_LIT` [LUNI.3.4]

> **Not v1.** This is the surface syntax of the `complex` type, which is
> deferred ([LUNI.14]). No v1 lexer produces `COMPLEX_LIT`, and `5i` is
> refused ([LUNI.14.9]), not read as a complex literal. Everything below describes the
> token as it will be when the type is built. It is kept in §3 beside the
> literal forms v1 does admit only because the `i`/`j` suffix reservation in
> [LUNI.3.1.5] is live and needs something to point at.

Complex number literals use a bare `i` or `j` suffix with no `_` sigil. These are
a distinct token class from unit literals:

```
COMPLEX_LIT ::= (INT_LIT | FLOAT_LIT | SCI_LIT) ('i' | 'j')
```

`i` and `j` are the same type and produce identical values (see §14). Display
convention is set at the module or interpolation site, not in the value. No lexer
ambiguity: identifiers cannot start with a digit, so `2i` is always `COMPLEX_LIT`,
never `INT(2) NAME(i)`.
